summary: LA County Forestry tower built spring 1930 to cover foothill haze; most foothill towers closed by early 1950s; listed as demolished; site now a hilly background.

facts.status_note: Listed as demolished by Angeles Adventures

events.note: Spring 1930 per Angeles Adventures; the county's 1931 annual report also describes the tower as constructed
Early 1950s; Angeles Adventures says most foothill county towers, this one included, were closed by then

evidence.supports: built spring 1930 northwest of the Pacoima warehouse
evidence.quote: In the spring of 1930, the Los Angeles County Forestry Department constructed a lookout tower on Pacoima Peak northwest of the Pacoima warehouse.

evidence.supports: 1931 annual report: purpose was haze over the foothills
evidence.quote: This tower was primarily established to overcome the haze situation along the foothills between Pacoima and Big Tujunga Canyons

evidence.supports: haze impaired views from Oat Mountain and Mt. Lukens
evidence.quote: which impairs visibility from both Oat Mountain and Mt. Lukens Towers

evidence.supports: 1931 annual report: peak is county property
evidence.quote: Lookout tower was constructed on Pacoima Peak, which is County owned property.

evidence.supports: November 1931 Forest Worker item: built on county property
evidence.quote: A lookout tower was constructed on county property on Pacoima Peak.

evidence.supports: most foothill county towers closed by early 1950s, Pacoima Peak included
evidence.quote: However, by the early 1950s most county towers along the foothills were closed including Pacoima Peak tower.
Smog had increased to such a point that visibility was decreased.

evidence.supports: site today is hilly background near airport, warehouse and Jessup Park
evidence.quote: Today, the lookout site is part a hilly background surrounding the Whitman Airport, the LACoFD warehouse, and Jessup Park.

evidence.supports: listed as gone, tower type, Los Angeles County
evidence.quote: Los Angeles Pacoima Peak 34.26355 -118.40831 Tower Gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Angeles Adventures and the Forest Lookouts 1930 entry give spring 1930; the 1931 annual report and November 1931 item describe the tower as constructed. These are consistent, so the story uses spring 1930 and cites the 1931 items as corroboration.

notes_for_editor: Ownership is 'unknown' in the record, but Forest Lookouts quotes the 1931 county annual report calling the peak county-owned property; consider setting ownership to county. No staff names were found, so staffing is left out. No photo with a usable URL was found; Angeles Adventures credits LA Public Library photos but links none. Angeles Adventures spells the airport 'Whitman' where the usual name is Whiteman; the story avoids the name. The demolition date is not given by any source read, so the story says only that the tower is listed as demolished. Record kind 'tower', agency and coordinates match the sources.
